digest.component_or_area: codebase comment taxonomy and documentation structure across six subsystems
propositions: ~2033 recoverable comment lines exist across 439 files in src/rebar, distributed non-uniformly across six subsystems (reconciler ~970 lines, others ~230 each) due to self-referential prose explaining an 800-LOC line cap.

Comment triage dispositions (RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE) must be applied to every unit, with load-bearing invariants (replay-compat, security contracts, anti-refactor warnings, lint pragmas) retained verbatim and recorded on do_not_move lists.

Verified-stale comments found at six sites contradict live code (e.g. P1-P9 floor vs 11 DET_CHECKS entries; stale Anthropic constraints; non-existent module paths), requiring correction in place rather than deletion.
Eight sites carry the same four-paragraph idempotent-transform rationale, necessitating consolidation into new ADRs 0062-0069 with inline citations replacing relocated prose.

Three files cannot be fixed by comment triage alone because their comments ARE the live invariants: event_append.py, _processors.py, and signing.py each recover <10 lines and their call-graph seams are out of scope.

Actual net recovery across six stacked shards is ~85 lines (not the ~2033 pre-triage estimate), because the work was correction- and relocation-dominated rather than deletion-dominated, with substantial prose moved verbatim into ADRs rather than deleted.
